proposals.evidence: DEDR5270 explicitly gives Tamil vā imperative of varu, Malayalam varuka, Kannada bar/bār with bā imperative, Kodagu bar-, Telugu vaccu, Parji ver- and Tulu barpini. These survey simple come responses retain the corresponding stems and ordinary endings; pronoun-led clauses and auxiliary constructions are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

These survey cut-/sut- hammer responses retain the attested family and ordinary suffixes. proposals.evidence: DEDR4316 explicitly gives Tulu poyyè sand and Malayalam pūyi sand, in the dust/powder family. Kudiya poya and Tulu poyya sand compare with this regional sand word. These forms are not among the bracketed ash forms that the article marks as probably Sanskrit loans. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4867 gives Tamil miḷaku, Malayalam miḷaku/muḷaku pepper, Kota meḷg chilli and Kodagu maḷu chillies. These southern survey forms preserve the pepper-to-chilli lexical extension explicitly attested within the family; the source chilli gloss is not changed to black pepper. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
